written.myAnswer: Cell → tissue → organ → organ system
Stomach epithelial tissue secretes mucus, pepsinogen, and hydrochloric acid.
Smooth muscles contract to churn and mix food with digestive juices and move it through the stomach.
Palisade mesophyll carries out photosynthesis.
The shoot system includes stems, leaves, flowers, and fruits. It supports above-ground growth and is involved in transport, photosynthesis, and reproduction.
Homeostasis is the maintenance of stable internal conditions, enabling cells and organs to function properly.
The body regulates temperature through responses such as sweating to cool down and shivering to produce heat.
A tissue is a group of similar cells performing a particular function; an organ consists of different tissues working together to perform a function.
The root system anchors the plant and absorbs water and minerals. The shoot system includes stems, leaves, flowers, and fruits and is involved in support, photosynthesis, transport, and reproduction.
Epidermal tissue forms the protective outer covering of a leaf; mesophyll is inside the leaf and is involved in photosynthesis and gas exchange.
Palisade mesophyll cells are closely packed and rich in chloroplasts, carrying out most photosynthesis. Spongy mesophyll has loosely arranged cells and air spaces that aid gas exchange.
Organelles form cells, cells form tissues, tissues form organs, organs form organ systems, and organ systems work together to maintain the organism.

The tissue level consists of groups of similar cells working together to perform a function. Plant tissues include epidermal, mesophyll, xylem, and phloem tissues; animal tissues include epithelial, connective, muscle, and nervous tissues.

The stomach contains epithelial, connective, and muscle tissues. Epithelium secretes mucus, pepsinogen, and hydrochloric acid; connective tissue supports the stomach and contains blood vessels and nerves; smooth muscle churns and mixes food with digestive juices.

The leaf has epidermal, mesophyll, and vascular tissues. The epidermis protects the leaf and stomata regulate gas exchange; palisade mesophyll carries out most photosynthesis; spongy mesophyll aids gas exchange; xylem transports water and phloem transports food.
Organ systems coordinate with one another to perform life functions and maintain homeostasis in the human body.

The digestive system breaks down food and absorbs nutrients and water. The excretory system removes metabolic wastes and helps regulate water and salt balance; together they help maintain stable internal conditions.

Roots anchor the plant and absorb water and minerals; stems support it and transport materials; leaves carry out photosynthesis and gas exchange; flowers are involved in reproduction; fruits protect and help disperse seeds.
The root system consists of roots, usually growing below ground. It anchors the plant, absorbs water and minerals from soil, and may store food.

Homeostasis is the maintenance of stable internal conditions, which is important for normal cell and organ function. Organ systems work together to supply and transport useful materials and remove wastes, helping maintain those conditions.

The respiratory system brings oxygen into the lungs and removes carbon dioxide. Oxygen enters the blood and is carried by the circulatory system to cells; carbon dioxide travels in the blood to the lungs for removal. This helps maintain suitable oxygen and carbon dioxide levels.

Epithelial tissue consists of closely arranged cells forming sheets that cover surfaces and line organs. Its structure suits functions such as protection, absorption, and secretion; stomach epithelium, for example, secretes mucus and digestive substances.

Organ systems work in harmony to supply and transport materials, remove wastes, and maintain homeostasis. Failure of one system can deprive others of needed materials or cause waste build-up, disrupting the body's functioning.
